title: IP-MT284-SnippetExpansionEngine

scope.summary:
GOAL: Add a VS Code / LSP-style snippet expansion engine to the native code editor — TextMate-syntax snippet bodies with tab-stops ($1, $2, $0), placeholders (${1:name}), mirrored/linked tab-stops (the same index appearing twice edits together), choices (${1|a,b,c|}), and a curated builtin set of variables ($TM_SELECTED_TEXT, $TM_FILENAME, $CURRENT_YEAR, $LINE_NUMBER, etc.). The MT-281 matrix marks 'snippet-expansion-engine' MISSING: the code editor has NO tab-stop/placeholder engine (the string 'snippet' appears only as search-preview text and a command alias), and the rich-editor slash_commands menu is a DIFFERENT surface (a command palette that inserts blocks, not a code-snippet template engine with tab-stop cursor sequencing). Snippet expansion also becomes the insertion mechanism LSP completion items of kind Snippet (editor_view CompletionKind) should use, and the apply target for a Snippet-format LSP textEdit.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: (a) NEW module dir src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/snippets/ with mod.rs, parser.rs (TextMate snippet-body parser -> typed SnippetAst), session.rs (SnippetSession: the live tab-stop cursor sequencer over the MT-001 TextBuffer + MT-003 CursorSet), variables.rs (builtin variable resolver), registry.rs (SnippetRegistry: builtin + language-scoped snippet definitions, loaded from a bundled snippets JSON, no network); (b) `pub mod snippets;` + re-exports in code_editor/mod.rs; (c) wiring in code_editor/panel.rs: Tab/Shift+Tab advance/retreat tab-stops while a SnippetSession is active (falling back to normal indent when none is active), Esc cancels the session, and an insert-snippet entry point the completion path (editor_view Snippet completions) and a future command call; (d) a bundled snippets/builtin_snippets.json (rust/generic) under the module; (e) unit + integration tests. PURE editor-side engine over TextBuffer/CursorSet; NO backend; NO network.

DETAILED SPEC — parity rule set (TextMate snippet grammar as VS Code implements it):
1. parser.rs: parse a snippet body String into `SnippetAst = Vec<SnippetNode>` where `SnippetNode = Text(String) | TabStop{ index: u32 } | Placeholder{ index: u32, default: SnippetAst } | Choice{ index: u32, options: Vec<String> } | Variable{ name: String, default: Option<SnippetAst> }`. Index 0 ($0) is the FINAL cursor stop (VS Code semantics: after the last real stop, the cursor lands at $0, or end-of-snippet if no $0). Escapes: \$, \}, \\ are literal. Malformed bodies degrade to literal text, never panic.
2. session.rs: on insert, expand the SnippetAst at the caret: resolve variables, materialize placeholder defaults, and build an ordered stop list (ascending index, $0 last) with each stop's live byte range. A SnippetSession holds the stops as MT-003 selections. Tab moves to the next stop (selecting its placeholder text so the operator types over it); Shift+Tab moves back; typing into a stop that is MIRRORED (same index appears >1 time) updates ALL its ranges live; reaching past the last stop (or $0) ends the session. Edits keep stop ranges correct via the buffer's byte-offset mapping (descending-order application discipline, the MT-051 line_ops precedent).
3. variables.rs: resolve the builtin set — $TM_SELECTED_TEXT (the pre-insert selection, enabling 'wrap selection in snippet'), $TM_CURRENT_LINE, $TM_FILENAME / $TM_FILENAME_BASE / $TM_DIRECTORY (from the panel's open-file path), $CURRENT_YEAR/$CURRENT_MONTH/$CURRENT_DATE (chrono, a workspace dep), $LINE_NUMBER, $CLIPBOARD (via the shared interaction_bus clipboard read — MT-031), $RANDOM/$RANDOM_HEX/$UUID. An unknown variable resolves to its default if present, else to empty string (VS Code parity), never an error.
4. registry.rs: SnippetRegistry loads builtin_snippets.json (a map of language_id -> [{ prefix, body, description }]) bundled in-crate. `resolve(language_id, prefix) -> Option<SnippetDef>`. Language scoping reuses the MT-071 language_mode LanguageId. NO user-snippet file IO in this MT (that is a later settings concern); the registry is bundled + in-memory.
5. LSP integration: editor_view completion items of CompletionKind::Snippet insert via this engine (their insertText is a snippet body); a plain-text completion inserts literally as today. Expose `SnippetEngine::insert(panel, body, language_id)` as the single entry the completion path and a command call use.
6. AccessKit / VIS: while a SnippetSession is active, each tab-stop selection is a MT-003 Role::Caret/selection (already emitted); add a subtle active-stop decoration (theme token, not hardcoded) so the operator can see which stop is active. No new heavy widget.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read code_editor/buffer.rs (TextBuffer byte-addressed edits), cursor.rs (CursorSet, Cursor anchor/head selections, MAX_ACCESSKIT_CURSORS), line_ops.rs (descending-offset multi-edit + single-undo-at-boundary precedent), editor_view.rs (CompletionItem/CompletionKind::Snippet insertion point), language_mode.rs (LanguageId), interop interaction_bus clipboard read (for $CLIPBOARD), panel.rs (Tab handling, insert path, undo boundary via interop_adapter push).
2. Create snippets/parser.rs + the SnippetAst types; unit-test the grammar: tab-stops, placeholders, nested placeholder defaults, mirrored index, choices, variables, escapes, malformed-degrades-to-literal.
3. Create snippets/variables.rs (builtin resolver) + snippets/registry.rs (bundled JSON load + resolve) + snippets/session.rs (the tab-stop sequencer over TextBuffer/CursorSet).
4. Wire panel.rs: Tab/Shift+Tab advance/retreat while a session is active (else normal indent), Esc cancels, mirrored-stop live update, whole snippet insert = ONE undo entry (line_ops single-undo pattern).
5. Wire editor_view Snippet-kind completions to SnippetEngine::insert.
6. Register `pub mod snippets;` + re-exports; ship builtin_snippets.json.
7. Integration test: insert 'fn' snippet -> Tab cycles name -> params -> body -> $0; a mirrored-index snippet edits both sites; ${1|pub,pub(crate)|} choice; $TM_SELECTED_TEXT wraps a selection; the whole insert undoes in one Ctrl+Z. Capture Argus evidence of an active session with the active-stop decoration.
8. Update the UserManual (same change): snippets — how to trigger, Tab/Shift+Tab to move stops, placeholders/choices/mirrors, builtin variables, and that snippet completions come from LSP + the bundled set.
forbidden_paths: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_editor/slash_commands/** (slash commands are a distinct block-insert menu, not the code-snippet engine)
acceptance_criteria: code_editor/snippets/ exists with parser.rs (TextMate body -> SnippetAst: Text/TabStop/Placeholder/Choice/Variable, $0 final, escapes handled, malformed degrades to literal), session.rs (tab-stop sequencer over TextBuffer/CursorSet), variables.rs (builtin resolver), registry.rs (bundled builtin_snippets.json + language-scoped resolve).
Tab/Shift+Tab advance/retreat tab-stops while a SnippetSession is active (placeholder text selected for type-over) and fall back to normal indent when no session is active; Esc cancels the session.
Mirrored tab-stops (same index appearing more than once) update ALL ranges live as the operator types; choices (${1|a,b,c|}) and nested placeholder defaults expand correctly.

Builtin variables resolve: $TM_SELECTED_TEXT wraps the pre-insert selection, filename/date/line/clipboard variables resolve from the real panel/file/bus state; an unknown variable resolves to its default or empty string, never an error.
LSP completion items of CompletionKind::Snippet insert via this engine; plain completions still insert literally.
The whole snippet insert is a SINGLE undo entry (one Ctrl+Z reverts it); byte ranges stay correct across edits (descending-offset discipline).
The engine is pure editor-side (grep-provable: no tokio/reqwest/backend/api import in snippets/**); an active stop has a theme-token decoration (no hardcoded hex).
UserManual updated in the same change: snippet trigger, Tab/Shift+Tab, placeholders/choices/mirrors, builtin variables.
proof_targets: cargo test -p handshake-native snippet_engine -- --nocapture 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok'

Argus evidence: argus.screenshot + AccessKit tree of an active SnippetSession (placeholder selected, active-stop decoration) after inserting a multi-stop snippet, stored under $HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT
expected_tests: unit: parse tab-stops, placeholders, nested placeholder defaults, mirrored index, choices, variables, escapes
unit: malformed snippet body degrades to literal text (no panic)
unit: $0 is the final stop; end-of-snippet fallback when absent
unit: $TM_SELECTED_TEXT resolves to the pre-insert selection; unknown variable -> default/empty
integration: Tab cycles stops in ascending order; Shift+Tab retreats; Esc cancels
integration: mirrored-index edit updates all sites live
integration: whole insert is one undo entry; byte ranges correct after typing into a mid stop
integration: LSP CompletionKind::Snippet inserts via the engine; plain completion inserts literally
implementation_notes: Verified grounding 2026-07-21: code_editor exports TextBuffer (buffer.rs, byte-addressed), CursorSet/Cursor (cursor.rs, anchor/head selections, MAX_ACCESSKIT_CURSORS), line_ops (descending-offset multi-edit + ONE-undo-at-panel-boundary, MT-051), editor_view CompletionItem/CompletionKind (Snippet variant exists), language_mode LanguageId (MT-071), interop interaction_bus clipboard read (MT-031, for $CLIPBOARD). No snippet module exists; 'snippet' currently only appears as search-preview/alias strings.

Design basis (cite in code docs): the VS Code / LSP TextMate snippet grammar — tab-stops $1/$2/$0, placeholders ${1:default}, mirrors (repeated index), choices ${1|a,b|}, variables with defaults, backslash escapes.
The rich-editor slash_commands menu is NOT this engine: it is a block-insert command palette. Do not fold snippets into slash_commands; snippets are a code-editor tab-stop template engine.
chrono is a workspace dependency (used elsewhere for dates) — reuse it for $CURRENT_YEAR/etc.; do not add a new date crate. Whole-insert single-undo reuses the MT-035/051 panel-boundary undo pattern.

Cross-family seams (reference only): MT-287 AI ghost-text may also insert multi-line edits but is a distinct accept/reject overlay, not a tab-stop session; the two insert paths must not fight over Tab (ghost-text uses its own accept chord).

surfaces: active SnippetSession tab-stop selections in the editor body
snippet insertion via LSP Snippet completions

target_entries: Code snippets: triggering a snippet, Tab/Shift+Tab to move between stops, placeholders/choices/mirrored stops, builtin variables, and that snippet completions come from LSP plus the bundled set

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Snippet expansion is a local buffer edit; it emits no new business events beyond the ordinary edit/undo the panel already records.
The parsed SnippetAst, the resolved stop list, and the active stop index are exposed as structured state so a no-context model can trace why a tab-stop landed where it did.
Synchronous editor-side engine; no child process.

risk_if_missed: Without a snippet engine the native editor cannot expand LSP Snippet completions or offer templated boilerplate with tab-stop sequencing — a baseline professional-IDE affordance. Snippet-kind completions would insert broken literal '${1:...}' text, which is worse than absent, so the completion path also stays degraded.

risks: RISK-1: Range drift — after typing into an early tab-stop, later stops' byte ranges are stale, so Tab lands mid-token or the mirror updates the wrong span, corrupting the inserted code.
RISK-2: Malformed body panic — a snippet with unbalanced ${ or a bad choice list panics the render thread instead of degrading to literal text.
RISK-3: Undo fragmentation — the multi-part expansion records many undo entries, so one Ctrl+Z only removes part of the snippet, leaving broken code.
RISK-4: Variable injection — $CLIPBOARD / $TM_SELECTED_TEXT content is treated as snippet syntax (its own $1 re-parsed), letting pasted text hijack tab-stops.
RISK-5: Tab hijack — the snippet session swallows Tab even when inactive, breaking normal indentation.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Stops are maintained as live byte ranges updated through the same descending-offset discipline as MT-051; a test types into a mid stop and asserts all later stops + mirrors remain correct.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): The parser is total — malformed input returns literal Text nodes; a fuzz-style unit test with unbalanced/garbage bodies asserts no panic.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): The whole insert is grouped into ONE undo entry at the panel boundary (MT-035/051 pattern); a test asserts a single Ctrl+Z reverts the entire snippet.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Resolved variable/clipboard/selection VALUES are inserted as literal text, never re-parsed as snippet syntax; a test with '$1' inside $CLIPBOARD asserts it stays literal.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Tab is intercepted ONLY while a SnippetSession is active; a test asserts Tab indents normally with no active session.

research_provenance.source: Direct source inspection 2026-07-21 of wtc-native-editors-v1: code_editor/mod.rs has NO snippets module; grep for 'snippet' found only search-preview fields (knowledge_documents.rs, sidebar_panel.rs) and a command alias (command_registry.rs) — no tab-stop/placeholder engine. buffer.rs/cursor.rs/line_ops.rs/editor_view.rs (CompletionKind::Snippet)/language_mode.rs supply the substrate. Confirmed 'snippet-expansion-engine' is not covered by WP-012 (MT-001..108), WP-013/014 stubs, STUDIO, or WP-011. External design basis: VS Code / LSP TextMate snippet grammar.
corrections: The rich-editor slash_commands menu is NOT a code-snippet engine (it inserts blocks via a command palette). CompletionKind::Snippet already exists in editor_view but has no expansion engine to honor it — this MT supplies that engine, so Snippet completions stop inserting broken literal placeholder text.
